title: Backpressure orchestration and tenant safety layers for downstream resilience
creator: Marcus Rivera
description: Implement a multi-layered backpressure and degradation orchestration subsystem that protects downstream dependencies (Redis, Kafka, SQL) across multi-region deployments. The subsystem must provide per-tenant safety quotas, an admission controller at the API edge, coordinated circuit-breaker signals to downstream proxy layers, and progressive degradation tiers (full, cached-read, degraded-read, stub) driven by SLO breach signals and connection pool pressure metrics.
background: Recent incidents showed cascade failures when Redis/SQL pools saturated in a primary region and upstream services continued to fan out requests. Existing connection governors clamp at a host level but lack tenant-aware prioritization and global failover sequencing. This ticket scopes a resilient orchestration approach that uses scoring-based admission, short-lived eviction hints to connection pools, and a multi-region safety window to avoid unsafe double-failover.
acceptance_criteria: Admission controller enforces per-tenant soft quotas and global safety budget with configurable weightings
Circuit-breaker signals emitted as structured events consumed by proxy/connpool components (schema documented)
Progressive degradation tiers implemented and toggleable per-route via Console; canary rollout to 5% traffic in us-west-2
End-to-end tests that simulate Redis saturation and demonstrate <1% total-error-rate for high-priority tenants using degraded-read fallback
Monitoring dashboards (per-tenant p99 latency, conn-pool utilization, circuit-open-duration) in Console and an alerting playbook mapped to SLOs
tasks: Design admission token algorithm (tenant weight + SLA score + recent-error-penalty)
Add circuit-breaker event bus topic and protobuf schema for signals
Implement light-weight admission middleware in API gateway + SDK hooks for client backpressure retry metadata
Extend connection pool to accept eviction hints and implement graceful client draining API
Implement degradation tiers in runtime: cached-read fallback, stale-ttl reads, and stub responses
Create e2e chaos test simulating cross-region DB throttling
Instrument dashboards and SLO-based alerting rules
Prepare canary rollout plan and rollback criteria
risks_and_tradeoffs: Aggressive shedding reduces tail latency and cost but risks dropping high-value requests — mitigated by per-tenant scoring and reserve buckets for SRE/enterprise tenants
Coordinated multi-region failover increases complexity; safety window avoids dual-writes/dual-fails but can delay failover for some tenants
Stale-read fallbacks may surface correctness issues for some customers; we will gate tier assignment behind route-level opt-in and document consistency guarantees
Adding admission tokens increases RPC metadata and slightly more CPU at the gateway — acceptable compared to improved downstream stability
implementation_notes: Use a leaky-bucket shaped token per tenant keyed by tenant_id; tokens are adjusted by a background scorer using recent errors and SLO burn
Circuit-breaker state is eventually-consistent across region controllers via the event bus; controllers apply a safety window (default 30s) before promoting a remote region to primary
Connection pools support a new TTL-based eviction hint to progressively slim max conns for low-priority tenants without hard-closing active streams
Degradation tiers are encoded as orderable enums so runtime can progressively fallback; tier mapping stored in route config and surfaced in Console
Score calculation includes: tenant_priority(0-10), recent_error_rate(1m), token_cost_estimate, and configured reserve_cap
We will ship schema v1 for circuit events and reserve room for v2 telemetry fields
